deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1983 Teichmüller notes Grothendieck studies the 'special' 5-point configurations K on the Riemann sphere Σ, meaning the points of M_{0,5} with nontrivial stabilizer in S_5. These are the orbifold points of M_{0,5}/S_5, which matter for the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal(Q̄/Q). They come in three kinds: pentagonal (case 1°), square-pyramidal (case 2°) and bitetrahedral (case 3°). The previous page ended the holomorphic case (ν=2, which has moduli). It then began the antiholomorphic case: σ is an anti-automorphism of Σ preserving K. Since σ fixes a point of K (|K| = 5 is odd) and has finite order, it is an involution with fixed points. So σ is a real structure of conjugation type, conjugate to z ↦ z̄; the margin note 'σz = z̄' records this normalisation. The cases are sorted by |K^σ| ∈ {5, 3, 1}, i.e. by the conjugacy type of the involution σ|_K ∈ S_5 (identity, transposition, double transposition).

(a) K^σ = K. These are the ordinary real points M_{0,5}(R), of real dimension 2. This family contains the pentagonal configurations (regular pentagon on a great circle).

(b) |K^σ| = 3. Normalise the fixed points to 0, 1, ∞. Then K = {0, 1, ∞, λ, λ̄} with λ in the Poincaré half-plane (real dimension 2). This family contains the bitetrahedral configuration: equilateral triangle on the equator plus the two poles, λ = e^{iπ/3}.

(c) |K^σ| = 1, K^σ = {P}. The other four points I = K∖{P} are exchanged in two pairs by σ. Configurations {a, ā, b, b̄} modulo PGL_2(R) have real dimension 4 − 3 = 1. Choosing P on the real circle adds one more real dimension, total 2. This family contains the square-pyramidal configuration.

Bottom of the page: a table with three columns headed by trees (one vertex with 5 legs; two vertices; three vertices) and numbers '2 1 0'. The rows read 'nb comp. 1, 10, 15' and 'nb réalisations 12'. The column numbers 1, 10, 15 are simultaneously:
- the numbers of involutions of each type in S_5 (id, transpositions, double transpositions), i.e. the numbers of twisted real structures of types a, b, c;
- the numbers of boundary strata of \bar M_{0,5} (open part, 10 divisors D_ij ≅ \bar M_{0,4}, 15 points).
The arrows (bitetrahedral → column 10, pyramidal → column 15) show the columns are being used as types b and c. The '12' is the number of dihedral orderings (5−1)!/2, i.e. the 12 pentagonal cells of M_{0,5}(R). It also equals the number of labelled pentagonal configurations, 120/|D_5|.

Products written on the page:
- 10×3×2 = 60, +10×2×6 = 120, under column 10.
- 15×2×2 = 60, under column 15.
- NB: labelled pyramidal configurations 5×3×2 = 30 (apex, cyclic order of the square up to dihedral symmetry, chirality), equal to 120/|C_4|.
- Bitetrahedral configurations 10×2 = 20 (choice of the pole pair, chirality), equal to 120/|D_3|.
The 60/120/60 products look like cell or incidence counts for the twisted real loci or for the boundary of \bar M_{0,5}. Their exact meaning cannot be pinned down from the page. As incidences in the standard tiling of \bar M_{0,5}(R) they do check out: 12×5 = 60 edge–face, 12×5×2 = 120 flags, 15×4 = 60 vertex–face.

Purpose: to locate each special (orbifold) point of M_{0,5} on a real form twisted by an involution of S_5. This is presumably in view of the action of complex conjugation, and anti-automorphisms generally, on the Teichmüller tower and its relation to the Galois action.
errors: No substantive error. The dimension counts in all three cases are correct (real dimension 2 each, half the complex dimension of M_{0,5}).

In (b), fixing 0, 1, ∞ uses all of PGL_2(R), so λ ranges over C∖R. 'λ ∈ half-plane' is correct only after labels are forgotten or a component is chosen; with labelled points each transposition gives two components (upper and lower half-planes), consistent with 10×2 = 20 bitetrahedral points.
The products 10×3×2, 10×2×6 and 15×2×2 are not explained on the page. Their interpretation (component, cell or incidence counts) is ambiguous.

ideas.what: Classification of anti-holomorphic involutions of P^1 preserving a 5-point set by the induced involution in S_5 (|K^σ| = 5, 3, 1), giving three kinds of twisted real loci of M_{0,5}, each of real dimension 2.
ideas.modern_name: Twisted real structures / real forms of \bar M_{0,n} indexed by involutions of S_n (moduli of real pointed curves with conjugate pairs)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ceyhan (2007, moduli of pointed real curves of genus zero); real points M_{0,n}(R) by Kapranov, Devadoss, Etingof–Henriques–Kamnitzer–Rains
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,5}, the Teichmüller tower and 'anti-automorphisms' and complex conjugation in general terms; this explicit case split is not there as far as I know.

ideas.what: Locating each special (orbifold) point type of M_{0,5} on a real form: pentagonal on the untwisted one, bitetrahedral on transposition-twisted ones, square-pyramidal on double-transposition-twisted ones.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold points of M_{0,5}/S_5 as fixed points of anti-holomorphic involutions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the special points of M_{0,5} (pentagonal etc.) as generators of the 'Lego'.

ideas.what: Counts of labelled special configurations: 12 pentagonal, 30 pyramidal, 20 bitetrahedral (= 120/|Aut|), and of strata/involutions 1, 10, 15.

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically considers all real forms of M_{0,5} twisted by involutions of S_5 (not just M_{0,5}(R)). He matches each twisted real form to a special-point type: pentagonal ↔ id, bitetrahedral ↔ transposition, pyramidal ↔ double transposition. This lets the elliptic/orbifold points be studied through real geometry, presumably to control anti-automorphisms of the Teichmüller tower. The twisted real loci themselves were later studied by Ceyhan; the explicit pairing with the orbifold points and its use for the action of complex conjugation in the Lego is not something I can point to in the literature, but it is minor.
missed.quote: Quand K^σ = 3 ... K = {0,1,∞,λ,λ̄}, λ ∈ demi-plan de Poincaré ... Contient le cas 3° (bitétraédral)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Small relevance to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory with complex conjugation (the 'real' GT / dihedral versions of the tower). Mostly an early anticipation of twisted real moduli.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct but elementary classification of real structures compatible with 5-point configurations, with routine counts. It anticipates the twisted real forms of M_{0,n} studied later (Ceyhan) and links them to the special points of M_{0,5}, but nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Quand K^σ = 3' should read 'Quand |K^σ| = 3' (cardinality), and likewise '|K^σ| = 1' in (c).

Case (c): read roughly '(Σ, I) est un syst. de 4 pts dans une sphère complexe, dont σ réalise une [...] ("conjugaison"), ils sont bien connus et de dim. réelle 1, de plus le choix d'un pt P [sur le cercle réel] fait une dim. de réel supplémentaire, soit dim. réelle totale 2 encore'.
Final line of (c): '(Contient le cas pyramidal carré, 2°)'.
The struck-out note under the column 10 counts appears to read '(tétraédriques par / pentaédriques – pentagonales)'.
'nb réalisations ... 12' should be read under the first column; the arrows link 'pyramidales 5×3×2 = 30' to column 15 and 'bitétraédrales 10×2 = 20' to column 10.
The first line's 'M_{0,5}^! ≃ Sym_2^*(M_{0,3})' is uncertain from the image; the essential reading is 'les points réels de M_{0,5}'.
